To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) CRITICA is a program that uses comparative sequence analysis to predict protein-coding regions in DNA sequences; and 2) CRITICA performs better than the current state-of-the-art program, GENMARK.

CRITICA (1) identifies protein-coding regions in DNA sequences more accurately than GenMark, (2) is not biased by existing sequence annotations, (3) identifies more coding regions than GenMark, including many regions that would not have been predicted by GenMark, and (4) identifies more regions that are likely not coding than GenMark.

CRITICA (1) uses comparative analysis of DNA sequence to identify likely protein-coding regions in DNA, (2) is more accurate than Genmark, (3) is not dependent on existing DNA sequence annotations, and (4) is freely available.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and applying methods of comparative analysis of DNA and amino acid sequences for gene recognition.
the development and evaluation of computational methods for identifying protein-coding sequences.
developing a computational approach to the recognition of protein-coding sequences from genomic DNA sequence data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRITICA has been developed to provide an alternative to the current gene-finding programs and is a valuable addition to the existing tools for gene prediction in DNA sequences.
CRITICA represents an important step forward in the analysis of coding regions.
CRITICA represents a major improvement over the state of the art in the field of gene recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CRITICA can be applied to the analysis of any genome for which there is a related sequence in the database.
CRITICA provides accurate predictions of likely coding regions in novel genomes.
CRITICA has been developed to be a useful tool for identifying protein-coding regions in DNA sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CRITICA can be used to analyze novel DNA sequences, and it can be used to identify errors in existing sequence annotations.
comparative analysis can provide a powerful tool for gene prediction, especially when combined with other noncomparative evidence.
the comparative analysis of DNA and amino acid sequences can be used to improve the accuracy of gene prediction in prokaryotic genomes.
